patients.summary: Office administrator with poorly controlled hypertension, CAD with a 2016 LAD stent, and paroxysmal AF who joins in 2019. Essential tremor is diagnosed in 2021, CML in December 2021, and stage IV ascending colon adenocarcinoma in 2022, treated with hemicolectomy and capecitabine; flecainide toxicity in 2025 and a chemotherapy-induced pancytopenia later that year.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
56 yo man, office administrator, transferring care after his longtime PCP retired.

HTN for years, on lisinopril 20 and HCTZ 25. Home cuff readings he brought average mid 140s over low 90s. Says it has "never really been where they want it." Takes meds every morning, no missed doses he can think of.

CAD: had chest tightness with exertion in 2016, cath at an outside hospital, one drug-eluting stent to the LAD. Since then rare tightness with heavy exertion, settles with rest, unchanged for a couple of years. On metoprolol succinate 50, ISMN 30, aspirin 81.

Paroxysmal AF picked up in 2018 when he had a spell of fluttering; sees outside cardiology yearly. Occasional brief palpitations, nothing lasting.

Social: married. Former smoker, about 20 pack-years, quit 2013. 1-2 drinks a week. Jogs a couple of times a week.
Family: father HTN and an MI at 62; father also had shaky hands. Mother type 2 diabetes. One older brother, healthy as far as he knows.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 148/92 (repeat similar), HR in the 60s regular, BMI ~28. Well appearing. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Normal gait.

A/P
1. HTN, above goal on 2 drugs. Basic labs today. Will keep going with home log and revisit in 3 months.
2. CAD s/p LAD stent, stable angina - stable. Continue current regimen, cardiology following.
3. Paroxysmal AF - rate controlled on metoprolol, cardiology following.
4. Health maintenance: Tdap today. Hep C and HIV screen once - ok'd. Colonoscopy has never been done; discussed screening at length. He'd rather wait until after the busy season at work, will revisit. Qualifies for lung screening by pack-years and quit date - low-dose CT ordered. Shingrix at flu shot visit next month.

Records release signed. RTC 3 mo.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Brian, your labs from Tuesday look fine: kidney function, potassium and blood count normal, A1c normal, hepatitis C and HIV screens negative. Cholesterol panel attached. See you in December.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Received 46 pages from the patient's former primary care office (faxed). Includes visit notes 2014-2019, medication lists matching current, and a 2016 hospital summary: diagnostic cardiac catheterization for exertional angina, single drug-eluting stent to the proximal LAD, no complications, discharged next day. Prior office notes document routine labs, all unremarkable, and repeated advice to schedule a colonoscopy, never completed. Indexed and sent to PCP for review.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING. Baseline. Indication: former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 2013. Technique: low-dose helical acquisition without contrast. Lungs: no pulmonary nodules. No consolidation or effusion. Airways patent. Mediastinum: no adenopathy. Heart size normal; coronary stent and mild coronary calcification. Upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group, office visit 11/12/2019.

Dear colleague,
I saw Mr. Goodwin for his yearly visit. He has coronary disease with a drug-eluting stent to the LAD in 2016 and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation diagnosed in 2018. He describes the occasional tightness only with hard exertion, no change in pattern, and a few short palpitation episodes this year that end on their own. BP 146/90, HR 62. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema. ECG: sinus rhythm, normal intervals, no acute change.

Medications: lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, isosorbide mononitrate ER 30 mg, aspirin 81 mg. Allergies: none known.

Impression: stable angina; paroxysmal AF, infrequent and rate controlled. Plan unchanged; see him in a year.

Outside cardiology

BP today above goal, similar to home. Heart regular. No edema.

Annual exam. 57 yo. Feels well. Working from home, back to jogging 2-3x/wk. No chest tightness this summer. A couple of 10-minute palpitation spells, self-limited.
ROS otherwise neg.
Meds unchanged (lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, metoprolol succ 50, ISMN 30, ASA 81). NKDA.

- HTN: home average ~143/90. He'd still like to try harder on lifestyle before adding anything. BMP today.
- CAD/stable angina, pAF: stable, cardiology in Nov.
- CRC screening: still declines colonoscopy for now; agreed to a FIT kit, mailed from here.
- Lung screening: annual LDCT ordered.
- Lipids, A1c, CBC today. Flu shot given.
- PHQ-2 negative.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Shaky hands since around October, both sides. Notices it holding his coffee and signing things; coworkers have commented. Says a beer in the evening calms it. No falls, no change in walking, no voice change. No new meds. Caffeine 2 cups/day.
BP still above goal. Fine bilateral tremor with arms outstretched, less at rest. Finger-nose ok. Normal tone, normal rapid alternating movements, gait normal.
A/P: bilateral action tremor, sounds like essential tremor (father had a tremor too) but would like neurology to confirm. TSH and BMP today. Referral placed. He's already on a beta-blocker for his heart.
HTN unchanged, discussed again, he wants to wait.

documents.title: Thyroid and kidney tests

documents.title: Neurology consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology practice. Date of service: 04/14/2021.
Reason for referral: hand tremor.

HPI: 58-year-old right-handed man with six months of tremor in both hands. It is most noticeable when he holds a cup of coffee or writes, and he has noticed it lessens after a drink. No head trauma and no seizures. No stiffness or slowness.

PMH: hypertension, coronary artery disease with LAD stent, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.
Medications: lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide for blood pressure; also metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, isosorbide mononitrate ER 30 mg daily.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family history: his father had a tremor of the hands; no other movement disorder in the family.
Social: office administrator. Former smoker (quit 2013, 20 pack-years). One to two drinks a week.

Exam: BP 142/88. Alert, fluent. Cranial nerves intact. Postural tremor of both upper extremities, low amplitude, symmetric, with mild kinetic component on finger-nose. No rest tremor. Tone normal, no rigidity. No bradykinesia on finger taps. Strength, reflexes and sensation normal. Gait and tandem normal.

Data: recent routine labs and TSH from his primary care office normal.

Impression: essential tremor.
Plan: reassurance; he is already on a beta-blocker (metoprolol succinate) for cardiac reasons, and he does not want another medication now. Discussed adaptive strategies for writing and cups. Return as needed.

Outside neurology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to go over whether he'd qualify for the outside study of a new blood pressure medicine (saw the notice in our newsletter). BP has run above goal for the whole time I've known him on lisinopril 20 + HCTZ 25, home average about 145/91.
Neurology saw him for the tremor, essential tremor, no new medicine.
Went through the study criteria with him: uncontrolled pressure on 1-2 agents, stable cardiac disease - he fits on paper, final eligibility is the study team's call. Explained it is randomized and blinded, so he might get the study drug or a placebo on top of his usual pills, and that he keeps all his current medicines. Visits at the study site for 6 months. He'd like to do it.
Exam: BP above goal. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema.
A/P: HTN uncontrolled. Referral letter and recent labs sent to the study coordinator. Will see him for the baseline visit.

reports.study: 12-lead ECG
reports.text: 12-lead ECG. Rate 62. Normal sinus rhythm. PR 168 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 418 ms. Normal axis. No ST-T abnormality.
reports.conclusion: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal ECG.

documents.title: Trial Baseline Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Baseline visit for the blood pressure study; the study team asked for a resting ECG and a chemistry from us. He was accepted and randomized last week to study drug or placebo, blinded; the site dispenses it and he takes it in addition to his usual lisinopril and HCTZ. Primary endpoint is change in systolic pressure at 6 months.
Feels well. No palpitations in months.
BP above goal (recorded for the site). ECG: sinus rhythm, normal.
A/P: enrolled. No change in his own medicines. Baseline BMP today, results to the coordinator. He knows to call us or the site with any side effects.

documents.title: Study visits
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI the study wants me in every 4 weeks, last visit around Thanksgiving week. No problems with the pills so far. Do I need to tell the pharmacy?

documents.title: RE: Study visits
documents.author: RN
documents.body: No need to tell the pharmacy since the study supplies it. Just keep taking your regular medicines the same way. Thanks for the update.

orders.reason: Marked leukocytosis with left shift, anemia, thrombocytosis

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three months of steadily worse fatigue. Wife told him he looks pale. Night sweats several nights a week, a few evenings of 99-100 F. Weight down about 6 kg since the physical without dieting. No cough, no urinary symptoms, no bleeding he's noticed, no chest pain. Off the study drug since 11/23.
Exam: pale. Weight 83 kg (89 in Sept). No lymphadenopathy in neck/axillae. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, nontender, LUQ hard to assess with his body habitus. No rash or bruising.
A/P: constitutional symptoms with pallor. CBC with smear review and CMP now, stat.

Addendum 16:30: WBC 64.0 with a left shift - lab smear review shows metamyelocytes and promyelocytes. Hgb 8.5. Platelets 600. Called hematology on-call; urgent consult arranged for next week. Patient called (see phone note).

documents.title: Abnormal blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with CBC. Explained the white count is very high with immature cells, he is anemic and platelets high - this needs a blood specialist promptly; could be a bone marrow problem such as a leukemia, and they will sort out exactly what. Hematology/oncology appt Fri 12/10 at 10 am. ED precautions for fever over 101, bleeding, chest pain or fainting. He understood; wife on speaker.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily with food and a full glass of water

documents.title: Hematology/Oncology consultation
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
Outside hematology/oncology clinic. Date of service: 12/10/2021, with marrow results 12/14/2021.

Referred for leukocytosis with left shift, anemia and thrombocytosis.

HPI: 58-year-old man, three months of progressive fatigue, pallor, unintentional weight loss, night sweats and intermittent low-grade fevers.

PMH: hypertension, CAD with LAD stent 2016, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, essential tremor.
Medications: lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, isosorbide mononitrate ER 30 mg daily.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family history: father with hypertension, essential tremor and MI at 62; mother with type 2 diabetes.
Social: office administrator; former smoker, quit 2013; 1-2 drinks weekly.

Exam: HR 104. Pale conjunctivae. Spleen palpable below the left costal margin. No lymphadenopathy. Heart: mild tachycardia, regular. Lungs clear.

Labs: hemoglobin 8.5 g/dL; leukocytosis with left shift including metamyelocytes and promyelocytes; platelets 600,000/uL.

Bone marrow aspirate and biopsy (12/10/2021): hypercellular marrow with increased granulopoiesis; blasts not increased. BCR-ABL1 fusion detected by FISH and quantitative PCR.

Impression: chronic myeloid leukemia, BCR-ABL1 positive, chronic phase.

Plan: imatinib 400 mg daily started 12/14/2021 via our specialty pharmacy. CBC every 2 weeks initially, quantitative BCR-ABL1 every 3 months. Reviewed side effects (fluid retention, cramps, nausea, rash, cytopenias). Return in 4 weeks.

Outside hematology/oncology

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, pt at home. Hematology confirmed CML, chronic phase; on imatinib 400 daily since 12/14. A little queasy if he takes it without food, otherwise fine. Still tired, sweats a bit less. Lots of questions - went over what chronic phase means and that hematology will follow counts and the BCR-ABL level.
Med list updated with imatinib. Reminded him to run any new medicines or supplements past hematology because of interactions.
Vaccines: due for pneumococcal now that he's on cancer treatment - PCV20 at a nurse visit in January.
HTN, CAD, pAF unchanged. Study finished.
RTC 3 months, sooner prn.

documents.title: PCV20
documents.author: RN
documents.body: PCV20 given L deltoid, single dose, no further pneumococcal doses needed. Pt says energy a little better, sweats gone. Tolerating imatinib with breakfast.

documents.title: Hematology/Oncology follow-up
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
Outside hematology/oncology clinic. Date of service: 03/22/2022.

CML, chronic phase, on imatinib 400 mg daily since 12/14/2021. Energy improving, night sweats resolved. Spleen no longer palpable.

CBC today: hemoglobin 13.4, WBC 7.6, platelets 286, normal differential.
Quantitative BCR-ABL1 (IS), 3 months: 7.1%.

Assessment: complete hematologic response; early molecular response on track.
Plan: continue imatinib 400 mg daily. CBC monthly, BCR-ABL1 every 3 months.

Outside hematology/oncology

orders.reason: 3 months minimal rectal bleeding; never had colorectal screening

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Since about February he's seen a little bright red blood on the paper after BMs, maybe once a week. No pain, no change in his bowel pattern, no blood in the bowl. Weight back up (86 kg). Feeling much better since starting imatinib; hematology says his counts are normal now.
Exam: BP above goal. Abdomen soft, nontender, no mass. Declined rectal exam today, prefers GI do it.
A/P: minimal rectal bleeding, likely hemorrhoidal but he is 59 and has never been screened - GI referral for evaluation and colonoscopy. He agrees this time. BMP today for his BP meds. HTN otherwise unchanged.

documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology group. Date of service: 06/13/2022.

Reason: rectal bleeding.

HPI: 59-year-old man with chronic myeloid leukemia on imatinib, referred for about three months of small amounts of bright red blood seen on the tissue after bowel movements. No significant pain, no change in bowel habit, no weight loss. Has never had a colonoscopy.

PMH: hypertension, controlled per patient on lisinopril; CAD with LAD stent; paroxysmal atrial fibrillation; essential tremor; CML.
Medications: lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, aspirin 81 mg, isosorbide mononitrate ER 30 mg, imatinib 400 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: no colorectal cancer in the family.
Social: former smoker; occasional alcohol.

Exam: external hemorrhoids. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. Digital rectal exam: no blood on the examining finger; prostate nontender, normal size.

Impression: minimal outlet-type bleeding with external hemorrhoids; colonoscopy indicated given his age, no prior screening and the bleeding.
Plan: colonoscopy with split-dose prep, scheduled 6/28. Hold aspirin not required. Fiber supplement.

Outside gastroenterology

reports.study: Surgical pathology report
reports.text: SURGICAL PATHOLOGY. Specimen: ascending colon mass, cold forceps biopsies (6 fragments). Microscopic: invasive gland-forming adenocarcinoma with desmoplastic stroma, moderately differentiated.
reports.conclusion: Ascending colon, biopsy: invasive adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated.

documents.title: Colonoscopy report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology endoscopy unit. Procedure date: 06/28/2022.
Indication: rectal bleeding; no prior screening.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care. Prep: good (BBPS 8).
Findings: cecum reached, appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve photographed. A friable, partly circumferential mass about 4 cm in the ascending colon, non-obstructing; biopsied and tattooed distally. Remainder of the colon normal. Retroflexion: small hemorrhoids.
Impression: ascending colon mass, suspicious for malignancy. Hemorrhoids.
Plan: await pathology; CT staging; surgical referral.

Addendum 06/30/2022: pathology shows invasive adenocarcinoma. Patient informed by phone; CT chest/abdomen/pelvis and colorectal surgery consultation arranged.

Outside gastroenterology

documents.title: Colon biopsy result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Brian after GI's report came in. He already knows it's cancer from GI yesterday. Shaken but has a plan: CT next week, surgeon visit after. Answered questions about how this fits with the CML - two separate problems; hematology already aware. Told him we're here and to message any time. Will see him after surgery.

reports.study: CT chest
reports.text: CT CHEST WITH CONTRAST. Indication: staging, colon adenocarcinoma. Lungs clear without nodules or masses. No effusion. No mediastinal, hilar or axillary adenopathy. Heart normal in size; coronary stent.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of thoracic metastatic disease.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST. Focal circumferential wall thickening of the ascending colon at the site of the known mass, with a few subcentimeter adjacent mesenteric nodes. Two subcentimeter hypodensities in the liver, too small to characterize. Spleen normal in size. Kidneys, adrenals, pancreas unremarkable. No ascites. Bladder and prostate unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Ascending colon mass. Two subcentimeter liver hypodensities, too small to characterize; MRI could be considered.

documents.title: CT staging reports received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: CT chest and CT abdomen/pelvis reports from the outside imaging center (exam date 07/06/2022) received by fax, scanned, routed to PCP.

events.reason: Laparoscopic right hemicolectomy for ascending colon adenocarcinoma

reports.study: Surgical pathology report
reports.text: SURGICAL PATHOLOGY. Specimen: right colon and terminal ileum, laparoscopic right hemicolectomy. Tumor: ascending colon, 4.2 cm, adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, invading through the muscularis propria into pericolonic tissue. Lymphovascular invasion not identified. Margins (proximal, distal, radial) negative. Lymph nodes: 2 of 18 positive for metastatic carcinoma.
reports.conclusion: Adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon, pT3 N1b, margins negative.

procedures.procedure: Laparoscopic right hemicolectomy with primary anastomosis

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: colorectal surgery
documents.body:
Outside regional hospital, colorectal surgery service. Admitted 07/21/2022, discharged 07/24/2022.

Diagnosis: adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon.
Procedure: laparoscopic right hemicolectomy with primary stapled ileocolic anastomosis, 07/21/2022. Uncomplicated.

Course: enhanced recovery pathway. Clear liquids day 0, diet advanced day 1, flatus day 2, bowel movement day 3. Pain controlled with acetaminophen and minimal opioid. Incisions clean. Ambulating independently. Aspirin continued; imatinib held 7/20 to 7/23 and resumed at discharge per hematology.

Pathology (final 07/26): pT3 N1b (2/18 nodes), margins negative.

Discharge medications: lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, isosorbide mononitrate ER 30 mg daily, imatinib 400 mg daily; acetaminophen as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: colorectal surgery 2 weeks; medical oncology referral placed; MRI liver to characterize the CT liver lesions.

Outside colorectal surgery

documents.title: Post-Discharge Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 5 days after discharge from laparoscopic R hemicolectomy (7/21). Eating normal meals, BMs daily and soft, incision soreness only. No fever. Walking a mile a day. Back on imatinib.
Path: pT3 N1b, margins clear. Liver MRI 8/10 for the two small spots on CT, then oncology.
Exam: afebrile. BP above goal as usual. Port sites clean, dry, no erythema. Abdomen soft, appropriately tender near the extraction incision. No edema.
Meds reconciled against the discharge list - unchanged plus acetaminophen prn.
A/P: recovering well after hemicolectomy for colon adenocarcinoma. Oncology and MRI scheduled. CML on imatinib. HTN - continue. Spent time on what node-positive means and why the MRI matters. Message us with results.

Plan: capecitabine 1500 mg by mouth twice daily on days 1-14 of each 21-day cycle, cycle 1 starting 09/06/2022. Continue imatinib 400 mg daily; hematology following. CBC and CMP each cycle, CEA, CT chest/abdomen/pelvis every 3-4 months. Hand-foot care and diarrhea instructions given.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Outside regional hospital emergency department. Visit 04/08/2025, 07:05-12:20.

CC: palpitations and lightheadedness.
HPI: 62-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, poorly controlled hypertension, CAD with LAD stent, essential tremor, CML on imatinib and colon cancer on capecitabine, who felt sudden rapid heartbeat and lightheadedness about 20 minutes into a morning jog. No syncope, no chest pain. Takes flecainide 100 mg twice daily (cardiology, since 11/2024) and metoprolol.
Home medications (per pharmacy list): lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, aspirin 81 mg, isosorbide mononitrate ER 30 mg, imatinib 400 mg, capecitabine 1500 mg twice daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father HTN, essential tremor, MI at 62; mother type 2 diabetes; older brother colorectal cancer at 61.
Social: former smoker, quit 2013, 20 pack-years; 1-2 drinks a week; office administrator.

Exam on arrival: BP 130/85, HR 160 irregular, RR 18. Anxious, alert. Lungs clear. No edema. Neuro nonfocal.
Labs: sodium 140 mEq/L, potassium 4.2 mEq/L, creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, troponin I <0.01 ng/mL.
ECG: atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response and a widened QRS. His earlier ECGs show atrial fibrillation with a normal QRS.

MDM: exertional rapid AF with rate-related QRS widening on a class IC agent - consistent with flecainide adverse effect. Flecainide held. On continuous monitoring his rate slowed and he converted spontaneously to sinus rhythm at about 11:40 with a narrow QRS on repeat ECG. Asymptomatic afterward.

Disposition: discharged home 12:20. Stop flecainide until seen by cardiology. Continue metoprolol. No jogging until cleared. Cardiology follow-up within 2 weeks; primary care within a week.
Diagnoses: atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; flecainide adverse effect.

reports.study: Bone marrow pathology report
reports.text: BONE MARROW ASPIRATE AND CORE BIOPSY, posterior iliac crest. Clinical: CML on imatinib, colon adenocarcinoma on capecitabine, new pancytopenia. Core: hematopoietic precursors of all lineages show markedly increased apoptotic bodies. Immunohistochemistry: increased p53 and BAX expression in hematopoietic precursors. Blasts not increased (CD34 under 2%). No metastatic carcinoma. Aspirate: maturing trilineage elements with increased apoptotic forms; no dysplasia.
reports.conclusion: Marrow with markedly increased precursor apoptosis, consistent with cytotoxic therapy effect. No increase in blasts; no evidence of CML progression. No metastatic carcinoma.

Interval: chemotherapy-related pancytopenia last fall, recovered; capecitabine resumed at 1000 mg BID d1-14 q21d. Flecainide stopped April 2025 after the ED visit; no AF since. CT Feb stable; next CT this summer with oncology.
Feels well. Working, walking and jogging easy miles. Tremor unchanged.
Meds: lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, metoprolol succinate 50, ISMN 30, ASA 81, imatinib 400 daily, capecitabine 1000 BID d1-14 q21d. NKDA.
Exam: BP above goal. Well appearing. HEENT normal. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft, healed incisions, no mass. No edema. Skin without bruising. Mild postural tremor.
